scope: Public literature, computational reanalyses and explicitly labeled synthetic software checks only. Wet-lab validation is deferred. No private genomic data are included. The GSE65145 summary and N1002K equal-expression audit were checked by the research assistant for source support, privacy and scientific limits; neither has received independent human scientific review. The immunotherapy audit is assistant-reviewed, not independently human-reviewed, and distinguishes tumor control from BUB1B disease rescue.

records.title: 704-drug NMD screen: reporter specificity
records.model: Published mouse Neuro-2a AS-NMD isoform summaries; three reporter genes, not BUB1B.
records.finding: Montelukast has a published permutation q of 0.021150, but the response is reporter-dependent and confounded by non-NMD isoform changes. No hit establishes functional BUBR1 rescue.
limitations: Normalized RNA ratios cannot isolate decay from splicing or isoform regulation.
Replicate Ct values are unavailable. Published ratio SEM formulas do not provide valid replicate-based uncertainty; no error bars are shown.
Translation inhibition is counterevidence for homoharringtonine. Statistical significance is not therapeutic suitability.
records.next: Establish L737* residual function first; any NMD candidate then needs allele-specific RNA, protein synthesis, and separate checkpoint/segregation endpoints.

records.title: L737* readthrough: exact versus nearby contexts
records.model: Published 144-nt PTC reporters in human cells; nearest-context subset, not endogenous BUB1B.
records.finding: No exact L737* measurement or exact six-flanking-base match in the 5,837-PTC table. Twelve nearest contexts have a median paired gentamicin increment of 0.0165 percentage points.
limitations: Neighboring-context values are not a prediction for L737* or the child.
The main predictive analysis excluded gentamicin for weak signal.
Readthrough does not guarantee native leucine, endogenous transcript survival, or functional BUBR1. Gentamicin plus mefloquine remains an experimental branch only.
records.next: Use the exact L737* context with matched controls and independently test full-length protein, checkpoint response and segregation fidelity.

records.title: BUBR1 functional controls: arrest duration
records.model: Published HeLa BUBR1 depletion/replacement with WT or engineered TPR variants under nocodazole challenge.
records.finding: Figure 4B source-data medians are 650 minutes for WT and 60 minutes for D137R. A control for checkpoint competence, not a drug-rescue result.
limitations: D137R is not N1002K; no tested drug or exact patient genotype.
Cells in the displayed representative replicate are not independent biological replicates.
Mitotic-arrest duration under spindle challenge is not chromosome-segregation fidelity in unperturbed divisions.
records.next: Require independent checkpoint and chromosome-segregation readouts in future equal-expression assays.

records.title: N1002K stabilization: equal-expression gate
records.evidence: DIRECT-BUBR1 COMPARATORS / RELATED-VARIANT IN VIVO / TARGETED AUDIT
records.model: Published human-cell BUBR1 depletion/replacement studies, MVA fibroblast rescue and a mouse L1012P comparator model; none tests N1002K.
records.finding: No exact-N1002K functional experiment was located. I909T/L1012P checkpoint rescue at matched abundance makes an abundance-limited mechanism plausible, but equally expressed B56-binding mutants still failed chromosome-congression rescue and mouse L1012P showed allelic effects beyond total protein level. Stabilization remains conditional; no drug is promoted.
limitations: This targeted audit is not a systematic review; failure to locate an exact-N1002K study does not prove that none exists.
I909T and L1012P are comparator variants, not substitutes for N1002K.
B56-binding mutants lie in a different region and demonstrate only that equal abundance is not universally sufficient.
Mouse L1002P models human L1012P, not human N1002K.
Checkpoint-only rescue must not be relabeled as chromosome-alignment or segregation rescue.
The published 6% versus 13% titration is cell-line-specific, not a universal functional or clinical threshold.
records.next: At measured matched abundance, compare WT, N1002K and L1012P in one depletion-replacement system; report nocodazole checkpoint arrest separately from chromosome alignment and missegregation per completed division. Wet-lab work is deferred.

provenance.method: Targeted exact-variant search plus primary-study comparison of abundance-matched BUBR1 rescue and counterexamples; no biological simulation was executed.
provenance.verification: Primary-source claims were checked against PMID 20516114 Figures 2D/3/4D, PMID 23789096 Figures 2/4 and PMID 31738183 Figures 1-3. Artifact bytes were hashed directly. No independent human scientific review or biological efficacy validation is claimed.

records.title: L737* NMD-first: test truncated-protein function
records.model: Published 731X/753X BUBR1 constructs and a proposed exact-L737* validation design.
records.finding: A related 731X construct motivates testing whether L737* retains useful function when NMD is bypassed. The exact L737* experiment has not been performed.
limitations: 731X is a frameshift product with about 715 native residues, not a clean L737* surrogate.
NMD sensitivity is predicted, not measured for this child.
More nonsense transcript can increase nonfunctional protein; NMD inhibition does not itself remove a stop codon.
records.next: Test WT, clean L737*, 731X and 753X at matched abundance; advance NMD modulation only if the exact truncation retains useful function.

records.title: Rapamycin in human fibroblasts: BUB1B locus RNA signal
records.evidence: Public human perturbation data; descriptive locus-level RNA reanalysis, not functional rescue.
records.model: Normal 2DD fibroblasts: proliferative vehicle, 0.5% serum, or 500 nM rapamycin for five days; two biological replicates per condition.
records.finding: The primary BUB1B-spanning feature has a Rap/Pro mean ratio of 0.585706 (41.43% lower); reduced-serum/Pro is 0.186191. Three nearly full-span features give the same direction. This does not support an RNA-abundance-increase rationale for sirolimus in this model.
limitations: Unstranded genomic-span features, not direct BUBR1 protein measurements or validated mature transcript isoform estimates.
Three overlapping features are sensitivity views of the same locus, not independent biological replicates.
Two biological replicates per condition from one normal cell line; no MVA genotype and no donor-level replication.
Serum reduction is a useful control but is not matched to rapamycin for cell-cycle distribution; no causal proliferation adjustment is claimed.
Continuous 500 nM/five-day treatment; no washout, transient exposure, aneuploidy, mitotic checkpoint or rescue endpoint.
Published normalized RPKM values are used as deposited without re-alignment, count-based differential expression, an added pseudocount, p-values or rescue probabilities.
149122 rows were observed in each deposited track; the paper states 149135 probes. The 13-row difference is not resolved here.
This does not establish that BUBR1 protein falls, rule out post-transcriptional effects, or predict clinical harm or benefit.
records.next: Keep sirolimus conditional. Proposed: compare full-length BUBR1 protein and segregation errors per completed division after transient exposure and washout at matched cell-cycle distribution. Wet-lab work is deferred.

provenance.method: Parse six deposited hg19 RPKM tracks; require >=99% reciprocal overlap with RefSeq NM_001211.6; select minimum boundary-distance feature and calculate ratios of arithmetic means. Check all three qualifying features.
provenance.verification: All six coordinate arrays match; each has 149122 rows. Eighteen rows overlap the anchor and three qualify. GEO sample titles and artifact hashes verified. Complete reproducible package saved separately; no human scientific review or new biological experiment is claimed.

records.title: Readthrough combinations: endogenous-protein transfer gap
records.model: Published HEK293 PKD1 reporters and WT9-12 cells bearing endogenous PKD1 Q2556X; not BUB1B.
records.finding: G418/ELX-02 with or without mefloquine were studied beyond reporters, including endogenous PKD1 protein and withdrawal measurements. This does not establish gentamicin-combination efficacy or BUB1B rescue.
limitations: Different gene, stop context and functional endpoint; endogenous Q2556X is TAG, not the L737* UGA premise.
RNA abundance does not isolate NMD; protein after withdrawal does not establish BUBR1 function or systemic tolerability.
No exact-genotype rescue, native leucine incorporation or clinically transferable exposure is established.
ELX-02 is a future mechanistic comparator; this audit does not establish market-approved Track 2 eligibility.
Qualitative audit only; no new biological experiment, numerical reanalysis or scientific chart.
records.next: Keep gentamicin plus mefloquine experimental only; add ELX-02 to proposed mechanistic comparators, not the repurposing lead list. Require exact-L737* RNA, full-length protein and checkpoint/segregation outcomes after withdrawal. Wet-lab deferred.

records.title: Amlexanox: context-dependent readthrough evidence
records.model: Published CFTR cells, GDAP1 neuronal progenitors, NEFL motor neurons and mouse NMD reporters; no exact BUB1B model.
records.finding: Functional CFTR evidence supports investigating amlexanox, but negative NEFL rescue with neurite toxicity and context-dependent NMD responses prevent promotion to an established lead. GDAP1 immunofluorescence does not by itself resolve full-length protein. No exact-L737* rescue is established.
limitations: Targeted audit, not a systematic review. No exact BUB1B-L737* pharmacological rescue was located in the sources reviewed.
NMD susceptibility remains predicted for L737*. Readthrough need not insert native leucine.
No efficacy probability, universal abundance threshold, docking result or new numerical biological result is claimed.
No patient genome-scale data were accessed. No independent human scientific review.
Positive and negative neuronal studies differ in gene, cell state, concentration and exposure duration; they cannot define a BUB1B therapeutic window.
Historical oral-paste approval and serum exposure do not establish systemic MVA suitability.
records.next: Can exact-L737*-derived full-length BUBR1 be demonstrated at an exposure that also improves checkpoint and segregation independently of cytostasis? Require allele attribution, viability/proliferation controls and separate functional endpoints. Wet-lab validation remains proposed.

records.title: Immunotherapy: disease rescue versus tumor control
records.evidence: DIRECT-BUBR1 MOUSE ABLATION / OTHER-MODEL CAR T / CLINICAL ONCOLOGY / OUR INFERENCE
records.model: BubR1 H/H INK-ATTAC mice; separate aging/metabolic CAR T mouse models; early human sarcoma studies. No exact BUB1B variant model.
records.finding: Genetic senescent-cell ablation delayed selected phenotypes in BubR1-deficient mice; uPAR CAR T benefits came from other mouse models. HER2 CAR T and nivolumab/ipilimumab show limited antitumor signals in sarcoma, while nivolumab monotherapy lacked solid-tumor responses in ADVL1412. Tumor control does not establish BUB1B rescue. No exact-genotype immunotherapy rescue was located.
limitations: Targeted qualitative audit, not a systematic review or quantitative reanalysis. No new biological experiment or scientific chart.
INK-ATTAC is transgene-dependent genetic ablation, not immunotherapy. The uPAR CAR T study did not test BubR1-deficient mice or the exact human variants.
Senescent, aneuploid and tumor cells are not interchangeable. Selective antigen expression and preservation of essential tissue remain unresolved.
Clinical sarcoma responses do not establish MVA efficacy, tumor prevention or correction of chromosome segregation. Small, selected trials do not provide an individual success probability.
Experimental HER2/uPAR CAR T products were not identified as market-approved repurposing leads. Immune toxicity and conditioning limit transfer.
Some primary reports were accessible only as abstracts, indexed passages or figure captions; no inaccessible full text was represented as reviewed.
No patient genome-scale data were accessed. Review was performed by the assistant; no independent human scientific review.
records.next: Retain immune senolysis as future exploratory research, not the immediate BUB1B rescue lead. Does a relevant BUB1B model contain harmful senescent cells with a selectively targetable surface antigen while preserving normal/progenitor cells and tissue function? Wet-lab validation remains proposed.
